name: Wordtune
tagline: Rewrite selected sentences for tone, length, fluency, and clarity with side-by-side choices

pricing.basis: annual billing, per user per month
pricing.notes: Recorded as the advertised monthly equivalent on annual billing; monthly billing is higher.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 10 rewrites and AI suggestions/day; 3 AI summarizations/month; unlimited spelling and grammar checks
tiers.notes: The page labels AI generations as limited daily use but does not publish a separate numeric generation cap.

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.limits: 30 rewrites and AI suggestions/day; 15 AI summarizations/month; unlimited AI recommendations, spelling and grammar
tiers.notes: Annual billing price shown; the live public page did not expose the exact monthly-billing amount to the crawler.

tiers.name: Unlimited
tiers.limits: Unlimited rewrites, AI suggestions, AI summarizations, spelling, grammar, vocabulary, clarity and fluency
tiers.notes: Annual billing price shown; the live public page did not expose the exact monthly-billing amount to the crawler.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 10 rewrites and AI suggestions/day, 3 AI summarizations/month, unlimited spelling corrections and grammar checks; separate AI-generation cap not numerically published
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual advertised as 50% off); paid plans offer a 3-day trial that requires payment details and auto-charges afterward
pricing.hiddenCosts: No refunds; the 3-day trial converts automatically unless canceled. Academic/nonprofit discount is 30% but cannot stack with annual-billing savings.

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Wordtune, rewrite selected sentences for tone, length, fluency, and clarity with side-by-side choices. The hard boundary is browser and document integrations plus proprietary rewrite quality, plus polish, integrations, and proprietary language models.
coreLoopDIY: Open local text or Markdown, rewrite selected sentences for tone, length, fluency, and clarity with side-by-side choices, show a diff, and save or export without uploading the document.
requirements: optional OpenAI or Anthropic API key for semantic rewrites
whatYouLose: browser and document integrations plus proprietary rewrite quality
moatNotes: polish, integrations, and proprietary language models
ongoingBurden: model quality, extension compatibility, dictionaries, releases, and sync
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Wordtune because the paid tool is already present everywhere they write and its suggestions have been tuned across millions of documents. The recurring cost buys model quality, extension compatibility, dictionaries, releases, and sync, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: LanguageTool
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source grammar and style checker with desktop and server components.

alternatives.name: Apple Writing Tools
alternatives.desc: Proofread, rewrite, shorten, or change tone almost anywhere, assuming your Apple hardware made the guest list.

facts.install: Built into current macOS, iOS and iPadOS; enable Apple Intelligence and let the required models download
facts.engines: Apple on-device foundation models and, for harder requests, Apple Private Cloud Compute; optional ChatGPT is used for Compose
facts.dataFormat: Edits are applied to text in the host app rather than kept in a separate Writing Tools library; on-device requests stay local, Private Cloud Compute says request data is not stored, and optional ChatGPT receives the selected content
facts.gapVsPaid: It rewrites and changes tone, but it offers fewer side-by-side alternatives and less granular sentence-level control than Wordtune.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Apple Intelligence-compatible Apple hardware, a supported language/region and several gigabytes of downloaded models

alternatives.name: Page Assist
alternatives.desc: A browser sidebar that reads the page, rewrites the selection, and saves custom actions; your local model does the thinking.

facts.install: Install the extension from the Chrome, Edge or Firefox add-on store
facts.engines: Ollama, Chrome AI (Gemini Nano) and OpenAI-compatible local endpoints such as LM Studio or llamafile
facts.dataFormat: Chats, settings and other extension data are stored in the browser's local storage; only the optional share feature contacts the project's server
facts.gapVsPaid: It can rewrite selected browser text, but it lacks Wordtune's polished inline choices, fluency tuning, and consistent shorten-expand workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: The extension installs cleanly, but it still needs a running local model endpoint and browser-to-localhost connectivity

alternatives.name: Witsy
alternatives.desc: System-wide selected-text commands, reusable experts, a scratchpad, and document context; bring the model and skip the subscription.

facts.install: Download a desktop binary from GitHub Releases; macOS also supports `brew install --cask witsy`
facts.engines: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, xAI, Meta, Ollama, LM Studio, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Groq, Cerebras, Azure and OpenAI-compatible endpoints, plus optional image, video, speech, search and MCP providers
facts.dataFormat: Conversation history, experts, settings and document repositories live in the local application profile; local files are indexed locally, while prompts and retrieved context sent to a cloud model leave the machine
facts.gapVsPaid: It can create rewrite commands, but Wordtune's immediate side-by-side sentence choices and editor integration are more focused and predictable.
facts.setupBlocker: It is BYOK unless you install Ollama and a local model; system-wide commands also need OS accessibility permissions

alternatives.name: Writing Tools
alternatives.desc: Select text anywhere, hit a hotkey, and fix, rewrite, summarize, or obey a custom instruction without opening another tab.

facts.install: Use the portable Windows ZIP or macOS DMG; Linux currently runs from source
facts.engines: Gemini, native Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible cloud or local endpoint on Windows/Linux; the macOS port also supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, OpenRouter, Gemini, MLX and Ollama
facts.dataFormat: API keys and configuration stay on the device; the app does not retain writing or logs, and selected text goes only to the chosen cloud provider unless a local model is used
facts.gapVsPaid: It is close for hotkey rewrites, but it does not match Wordtune's polished inline alternatives, sentence controls, and cross-device hosted consistency.
facts.setupBlocker: You must supply an API key or install a local model; macOS needs Accessibility permissions, while Linux installation and Wayland support remain rough

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Advanced plan and a personal local editor DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Wordtune in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, and a small Rust filesystem layer; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: open local text or Markdown, rewrite selected sentences for tone, length, fluency, and clarity with side-by-side choices, show a diff, and save or export without uploading the document.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create a three-pane editor with source text, suggestion list, and accepted-result preview.
Implement deterministic checks for repeated words, sentence length, passive constructions, and typography.
Add an optional API-backed rewrite action that sends only the selected passage.
Show every change as an accept-or-reject diff and support undo.
Import and export .txt and .md while preserving headings and lists.
Persist user rules, ignored terms, and recent documents in SQLite.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a browser extension.
Deliberately leave out Office or Google Docs plugins.
Deliberately leave out collaborative editing and cloud sync.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
